drive._units_note: All speeds mm/s; motor_deadband is mm/s (stakeholder 2026-07-20): the smallest wheel speed that actually moves the plant, = outputDeadband(0.03 duty) / vel_kff(0.002) = 15 mm/s. Firmware/host convert to duty as needed; no code default -- config is the source of truth.

calibration._rotation_calibration_note: 125-007 (adjacent-sim-plant-rotation-calibration-for-angle-stop-move-overshoot.md): sim-plant-measured, NOT camera-measured -- these correct the SIM plant's own ANGLE-stop coast-down overshoot (WheelPlant's first-order tau=0.13s duty->velocity lag, TestSim/wheel_plant.h -- the wheels keep coasting for a beat after the stop threshold fires, same physical mechanism real hardware's own actuation lag produces, .clasi/knowledge/actuation-latency-delay-in-plan.md), NOT geometry/stiction (contrast tovez.json's own hardware fit). Measured at omega=+/-2.0 rad/s (square_tour.py's own runTurnMove() rate) against SimLoop.get_true_pose(): identity calibration overshoots by a roughly-constant +11.8..+13.0 deg for target angles >=45 deg (45->56.9, 90->103.0, 180->193.0), least-squares-fit over that range to gain~1.006/offset~12.1 deg. Verified after fitting: 90 deg lands at 90.2 (err +0.2), 180 deg at 179.9 (err -0.1); the fit is intentionally NOT tuned for very small angles (<45 deg), which square_tour.py never commands (every corner is exactly 90 deg) and which the coast-down model saturates nonlinearly toward zero anyway (15 deg identity-overshoot measured +6.5, not +13 -- a single affine pair cannot cover both regimes, and this ticket's only consumer needs 90 deg). Requires 125-007's own sim_configure_drivetrain() plumbing (sim_ctypes.cpp/sim_boot_config.py) to take effect at all -- editing this JSON alone was previously a silent no-op for the sim path (SimHarness's own App::RobotLoop never got setRotationCalibration() called before that ticket). Symmetric pos/neg because the sim plant has no directional asymmetry coded (WheelPlant's dv/dt model is sign-symmetric); confirmed by measuring both directions. NOT a substitute for tovez.json's own camera-measured hardware values -- see that file's own note for why hardware needs a DIFFERENT (negative-offset) correction for a different physical reason.

control._vel_gains_domain: duty [-1,1] (NezhaMotor MotorVelocityPid); NOT the old PWM-percent scale
control._neutral_note: NEUTRAL baseline (stakeholder 2026-07-18): this is the no-calibration profile, so the gains are the most vanilla usable set, not a tuning. vel_kp = 0.002 = 1/500: full duty at the plant's ~500 mm/s full-scale speed (duty = error / v_max, the plainest proportional normalization; a pure-P loop droops by design). vel_kff = 0.002 = 1/500 too -- the SAME vanilla inverse-plant slope, and the open-loop law itself: with the PID disabled (TestGUI PID checkbox) the motor drives duty = kff * velocityTarget, so kff=0 would make PID-off dead rather than open-loop. vel_ki = 0 (no integrator), vel_imax/vel_kaw = 0 (inert with ki=0; kaw=0 = anti-windup off). vel_filt = 1.0 (no EMA smoothing, raw measured velocity; NOTE: no live SET key -- build-time bake only). This config is the source of truth for the drive/control parameters -- there are to be NO tunable defaults in the source. (The former UPDATE 2026-07-20 sentence here, about a half-dozen sibling control.* heading/distance/model-tau keys, is moot -- those keys were deleted, 119-003 config-attic sweep, no living consumer survived 115-003's motion-stack excision.)

control._drive_calibration_note: duty_per_speed_* [duty/(mm/s)]: open-loop wheel calibration, the inverse of the measured plant gain (speed_sweep 2026-07-27: L ~560, R ~510 mm/s per duty; ceiling ~500 mm/s). Per-wheel because the two gearboxes differ ~10%. crawl_pulse [-1,1]: fixed pulse amplitude for sub-breakaway wheel speeds, Bresenham-dithered in App::Drive; 0 disables. Measured breakaway is 1-6% duty and state-dependent (src/tests/firmware/duty_min/RESULTS.md) -- the earlier 0.20 was sized against a duty_sweep criterion that the standalone prober disproved, so crawl ships OFF pending a re-measure of the low end.
control._wheel_correction_note: IDENTITY as of 2026-07-31 (stakeholder). The fitted values (tovez: gain ~1.47) were measured against a duty_per_speed that was itself wrong by ~1.6x, so the pair was circularly calibrated -- each fitted against the other's error -- and the correction ended up pointing the WRONG WAY: it divided a 150mm/s request down to 96 before the duty conversion, on a robot that was already under-delivering. duty_per_speed is now a baked measured constant (App::Drive::kDutyPerSpeed), so this affine stage has nothing left to correct and is held at identity. Do not re-fit it against duty_per_speed again; refit only against camera-measured travel, and say so here. gain 1 / intercept 0 = no correction.
control._wheel_controller_note: 130-004: App::Drive's unified three-timescale controller. This is the NO-CALIBRATION profile (see this file's own _wheel_correction_note above: wheel_gain/intercept held at IDENTITY on purpose) -- both Stage B fast-PID and Stage C bias-trim adaptation held at 0/disabled to match, so this profile stays a pure open-loop-map baseline with no additional correction layered on top.

estimator._estimator_note: 117 (predict-to-now estimator v1): weight_heading_otos/weight_omega_otos committed 0.0 -- stakeholder's encoder-only-v1 decision, OTOS fusion is wired but not yet trusted with any nonzero weight. staleness_ms=60.0 is 3x Devices::Otos::kReadPeriod (20ms): generous headroom over the OTOS chip's own read cadence, small enough to exclude a genuinely stale reading before the next cycle's fresh one arrives.
